Canadian Non Wood Fibre Symposium Receievs Boost Due to Stakeholder's Meeting

Canadian Non-Wood Fibre Symposium Deemed a Success; Canadian Hemp Farmers Get Lead Over US
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Montreal, CANADA – January 29th, 1998 – The Canadian Non Wood Fibre Symposium has received extra special boost thanks to recent the multi-party stakeholder’s meeting with Health Canada. The meeting was held in Ottawa on January 25th –27th to formulate regulations for the commercial cultivation of industrial hemp in Canada. Sotos Petrides, President of Wiseman Noble Sales and Marketing Ltd., participated in the three day talks and will make a special presentation regarding the outcome of this historic meeting as the finale of the Canadian Non Wood Fibre Symposium, being held today, January 29th, at the Palais de Congres in Montreal, Canada.

“We are pleased with Health Canada’s responsive approach to the needs and interests of Canadian hemp farmers,” says Petrides, co-producer of the event with the Technical Section of the Canadian Pulp and Paper Association. Over the last four years, Health Canada has slowly granted experimental licenses, and has confirmed that for 1998, Canadian farmers will be able to obtain commercial hemp licenses.

Featured exhibitors at The Canadian Non Wood Fibre Symposium include Kenex ltd., Domtar, Hempco/Golden Crops, Alberta Research Council, Bolton Emerson Americas Inc., Hill Agra Sales and Poland’s Institute of Bast Fibres. As well, the Symposium will be host to international guest speakers who will discuss the technical considerations associated with cultivation and processing of non-wood fibres for the pulp & paper industry.

Sponsors include Banque Nationale Du Canada, Crane & Company, and Commercial Hemp Magazine. “The Pulp and Paper industry is certainly interested in exploring the potential of these crops as fibre sources, adds Francois Blaine, Director of Media Relations for the Canadian Pulp and Paper Association. “We’ve been carrying out research work along those lines for a few year’s now, and the Symposium will give experts in the field the opportunity to provide those in attendance with considerable insight as to the feasibility of utilizing such plant fibres in our mills.”

This is the first of three events this year produced by Wiseman Noble dealing with hemp and other non-wood fibres. On February 6th in Melfort, Saskatchewan, Wiseman Noble is co-producing Discovery ’98 Agri-Food and Fibre Forum with the Agri-Food Equity Fund. On February 18th and 19th in Vancouver BC at the Vancouver Trade and Convention Centre, Wiseman Noble is producing The Commercial & Industrial Hemp Symposium II. Sponsors include Bank of Montreal, Kittyhawk Securities, Canadian Pulp and Paper Association.
